item.title: Re: Recommend a Canon
item.content:encoded:
For instance I've recently become very fond of 014, The Concrete Man.

Ah, I see. Well, from there, I would recommend AIAD. A very in-depth canon about A.I.'s doing various things, and the narrative present is very evident. Many good entries in this canon, with various storylines and memorable characters you grow attached to. Very high quality canon, would definitely recommend.

Sci-Fi elements are always engaging for me too.

Sci-Fi is pretty broad, however, one canon filled with Sci-Fi themes is Ad Astra Per Aspera. This is a very complicated canon all about humanity, its works, and various interplanetary features. I personally have read very little from this canon, but what I've seen is very high quality, and the amount of works present make this one lengthy read. Sci-Fi 110%!

Thanks for the recommendations, all

No problem, my pleasure!

item.title: Re: Recommend a Canon
item.content:encoded:
And so, I thought I'd ask what canons individual members would recommend for a starting point to a guy who mostly read random SCPs and Tales until now?

What are your interest when reading through SCP articles? Do you prefer heartwarming, horror, what?

Recommend a Canon

Well, off the top of my head, I would definitely name off Rat's Nest and The Man Who Wasn't There.

WHY you recommend it?

Rat's Nest: Take's common GoI's and shifts their perspectives in interesting and believable ways. Covers a very unique take on "The end of the world." Very engaging story, many unique entries. They all cover unique topics, and even within the canon, there is no "canon" pre se. You can read in any order you wish, and still get the topics. Very well made canon hub, and has some very interesting entries to boot. One in particular I would recommend from this canon is 1. This may be in the last era of the canon, but it covers many GoI's, as well as skips, meaning no matter what your interest are, you'll likely find something you like in this tale.

The Man Who Wasn't There: Quite the interesting concept, and the canon allows much more expansion then the GOI. Very interesting takes in all directions, and the way it was set up is some of the best. I'd especially recommend the more recent entries from canrencon, more specifically, The Man In The White Suit. Very interesting perspectives, and an engaging storyline.
